findings.problem: Commit 22858062 added a UUID check at the start of RaitWorklistCommandService.execute: `if (!uuid.test(input.targetId)) fail('RAIT.TENANT_MISMATCH', 404)`. The WORKLIST controller's collection commands pass fixed strings as targetId, not UUIDs. createSchedule passes 'schedule' (rait-worklist-commands.controller.ts:39-40) and createBatch passes 'batch' (lines 85-86). So every POST /v1/inf/rait/schedules and POST /v1/inf/rait/batches now returns 404 RAIT.TENANT_MISMATCH before authentication, scope, guards or persistence run. Two existing coordinator/secretary commands are disabled. This is a lost legal/operational capability and a regression against main, not an approved S1 limitation. The tests do not catch it. The unit suites (rait-worklist-corrective.spec.ts:32/58, rait-worklist-production-red.spec.ts:73) pass UUID targetIds instead of the controller's literals. rait-worklist-production/corrective e2e only check route metadata. The only HTTP create-batch test is the negative 'batch creation cannot include a case linked to another same-unit pool' (rait-p402-scope.e2e.spec.ts:993-1012), which expects 404 and therefore passes for the wrong reason. It no longer proves exact-pool qualification of caseIds through poolCaseSql (lines 538-548).
findings.recommendation: Apply the targetId UUID check only to commands whose targetId is a path id: publish-schedule, approve-batch, accept-batch-item, declare-batch-item-impediment, draw and reassign. Alternatively, have the controller pass a typed absent target for create-schedule and create-batch. Keep the payload UUID validation (poolId, memberId, caseIds etc. → 400). Add real HTTP+DB positives through the actual controller: a qualified coordinator creates a schedule, and a secretary creates a batch with an exact-pool case. Change the other-pool create-batch negative to set up an otherwise valid request whose only defect is the pool, and assert the poolCaseSql rejection without side effects.

findings.problem: accept-batch-item and declare-batch-item-impediment merge the route parameter :caseId into the payload as caseId (controller lines 141 and 172). The new payload UUID loop therefore returns 400 RAIT.VALIDATION_FAILED for a malformed path caseId. Malformed path identifiers elsewhere return a controlled 404, e.g. targetId here and assertCase/scope reads. This is a minor inconsistency in the malformed-path-id outcome, not a disclosure.
findings.recommendation: Return 404 for a malformed path-derived caseId and keep 400 for body ids, or record that 400 is the intended outcome. Add one HTTP negative for a malformed route caseId.
